findings.label: Focus lost on the new-message re-render path
findings.detail: The strip-only repaint is now focus-safe (pass-1 blocking finding is fixed), but loadThreadMessages() still does box.innerHTML = msgs.map(...) whenever a poll brings a NEW message. That destroys and recreates every chip in the thread, so a user sitting on a chip loses focus to <body> and the next Tab restarts at the top of the page. Narrower than the original finding (it needs a new message to arrive, not just a reaction change) but newly consequential because the rebuilt subtree now holds focusable controls. Fix: after the rebuild, re-focus the chip matching the (messageId, emoji) that was active, reusing the lookup refreshStrips() already performs.

findings.label: Add-button hit slop overhangs the bubble
findings.detail: .chat-reactions has margin-top: 4px and .chat-reaction-add is 32px tall, while its ::after hit slop is 44x44 centred on the button - so the slop extends 6px above the button box, i.e. ~2px into the bubble above it. The button is position: relative, so the pseudo-element paints over the bubble's non-positioned content and will absorb a tap in that band. Realistic impact is a link on the bubble's last line directly above the add button. Fix: cap the upward slop (e.g. asymmetric top/height) or raise .chat-reactions margin-top to 6px.

findings.label: Chip accessible name changes on activation alongside aria-pressed
findings.detail: chipLabel() appends 'Dodaj swoją reakcję' / 'Usuń swoją reakcję' depending on `mine`, so the accessible name changes on toggle while aria-pressed also carries the state. Screen readers announce both. Not incorrect, but the conventional toggle pattern is a stable name with aria-pressed alone carrying state. Cosmetic; no action required before release.

findings.label: DDL and aggregation never executed against MySQL
findings.detail: Carried over from pass 1 and still open: no database was reachable (no node_modules, no .env, no DB_PASSWORD, no mysql/mysqld/docker on PATH), so CREATE TABLE, the real GROUP BY and the DELETE/INSERT IGNORE are proven only as SQL text with bound parameters. The utf8mb4_bin collation trap is handled up front. Orchestrator task, not an implementation defect: run npm run init-db plus a two-account smoke test before release.

resolvedFromPreviousPass: 1 (blocking) - focus and aria-pressed announcement lost on every chip repaint: refreshStrips() now reconciles each strip in place via syncStrip()/applyChip(); surviving chips are mutated and never moved, the add button persists for the strip's lifetime, the picker grid is built once and only its aria-pressed updated, and a chip that disappears hands focus to the add button of the same message.
2 - pressed state signalled by colour alone: pressed chip and sheet button now add border-width 2px plus an inset 1px white ring, with padding reduced by the same amount so nothing reflows on toggle.
3 - unpressed chip border contrast: raised from rgba(0,0,0,0.10) (~1.25:1) to #868F99, measured 3.28:1 on #ffffff and 3.11:1 on #f8f9fa.

4 - no server-side throttle: 30 toggles / 10 s per user id via an in-memory fixed-window counter (pure reactionThrottleStep()), checked after validation and before any query, self-pruning above 500 entries, 429 'Zbyt wiele reakcji. Odczekaj chwilę', surfaced in the client toast with optimistic rollback. No new dependency.

5 - chat density: the add button is now a 32px circle with a 44x44 invisible hit slop (strip row 32px instead of 44) and is revealed on row hover/focus only under (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), using opacity so it stays in the tab order and the accessibility tree. Touch behaviour unchanged.

checklist.1_privacy: PASS - both read paths go through buildReactionList(), which emits exactly {emoji,count,mine} and drops off-allowlist or empty buckets; mine comes from MAX(r.user_id = ?) so no user id is projected. Toggle response is {success,action,messageId,emoji,reactions}. Log line carries messageId + action only.
checklist.2_no_notifications: PASS - the toggle handler and the thread-GET addition reference no notifications table, no ensureNotificationsTable, no sendPushToUser/webpush/notifyAnonMessage, no activity feed, no is_read write, and never call notification-text.js. The notificationText(...) hunks in the server.js diff are a concurrent task's work.
checklist.3_auth_and_participation: PASS - requireAuth on the new endpoint; participation re-derived via SELECT m.id, t.initiator_id, t.target_id FROM anon_messages m JOIN anon_threads t with 404 then 403 'To nie Twoja rozmowa'; the thread aggregate is WHERE m.thread_id = ? after the pre-existing participation check at server.js:2745.
checklist.4_sql: PASS - every reaction statement is pool.execute with ? placeholders and the emoji never enters SQL text; parseMessageId() requires /^[0-9]+$/ plus Number.isSafeInteger and > 0, so the id reaches SQL as an integer and '7abc', '-1', '1.5', '0', '1 OR 1=1' are rejected with 400 before any query. DDL is a static template literal.
checklist.5_emoji_allowlist: PASS - isAllowedReactionEmoji() is checked server-side from the shared module before the throttle and before any query; off-list values get 400 'Nieprawidłowa reakcja'.
checklist.6_toggle: PASS - UNIQUE KEY uniq_message_user_emoji (message_id, user_id, emoji) on an emoji column with COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, in both ensureAnonMessageTables() and init-db.js; DELETE-then-conditional-INSERT IGNORE is idempotent and the response is the recomputed aggregate.
checklist.7_performance: PASS - one grouped query per thread load fanned out by groupReactionsByMessage() (no N+1); INDEX idx_reaction_message (message_id) in both DDLs; the toggle re-read is scoped to the single message.
checklist.8_a11y: PASS with one non-blocking gap (finding 1) - real <button type="button"> throughout, keyboard reachable, aria-pressed on toggles, gender-neutral Polish aria-labels, in-place chip mutation so the state flip is announced on the activated control, dialog role + aria-modal + aria-labelledby, aria-hidden/inert while closed, focus to the first emoji on open, Tab trap, Escape close (double-fire guarded), focus return with an add-button fallback, prefers-reduced-motion honoured at both breakpoints including the new opacity transition, esc() on all interpolated values. Gaps: focus lost on the new-message innerHTML rebuild (finding 1), hit-slop overhang (finding 2), name-changes-on-toggle nit (finding 3).
checklist.9_polish_wording: PASS - gender-neutral sentence-case strings throughout (Wybierz reakcję, Dodaj reakcję do wiadomości, Dodaj/Usuń swoją reakcję, Zbyt wiele reakcji. Odczekaj chwilę, Nieprawidłowa reakcja, To nie Twoja rozmowa); neutral emoji names; plurals via plCount(n,'osoba','osoby','osób') with a numeric fallback; no dodal(a) or masculine-only forms.
checklist.10_forbidden_files: PASS for this task - formularz.html, formularz.js, notification-text.js, sw.js and app-theme.css show as modified in git diff --stat, but grepping their combined diff for reaction|reakcj|chat-reaction returns 0 lines (the sw.js hunk is a one-line CACHE_NAME bump to prezenty-v119). Reaction CSS is entirely in the new public/chat-reactions.css with nothing added to wiadomosci.html's inline <style>; the server.js footprint is five targeted additive edits, not a rewrite.
checklist.11_init_db: PASS - anon_threads, anon_messages and anon_message_reactions added to init-db.js (+46, -0) with definitions mirroring ensureAnonMessageTables(), CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS throughout, cross-reference comments in both files, and the three tables listed in the closing summary.
